summary.text: 问 means “ask” or “inquire” and is the standardized simplified form of 問. The received analysis of 問 links 口 with speech and assigns 門 a sound role, though the available comparisons do not independently establish that historical sound link.

formation.text: The received analysis treats traditional 問 as phonosemantic: 口 supplies a speech-related meaning, while 門 is assigned the sound role. Modern and reconstructed readings can be compared, but they do not independently establish the historical correspondence. In 问, 門 is written 门 as part of the simplified form.

components.text: In traditional 問, 口 is the meaning element, associating the character with speech. The analysis does not specify an earlier form for it.

In traditional 問, 門 is assigned the phonetic role in the received analysis. The available readings do not demonstrate the historical correspondence, so they do not independently verify that assignment.

sound_limitation.text: The available same-system readings allow comparison, but do not independently verify the received phonetic analysis or establish a regular historical correspondence.

sound.text: Modern Mandarin has 門 mén and 問 wèn; their different tones and vowels mean this current pair alone cannot establish the historical sound relation.
Baxter–Sagart gives 門 *mˤə[r] and 問 *C.mu[n]-s in its Old Chinese system. The comparison does not by itself confirm the component analysis.

components.text: In 问, 门 is the simplified form corresponding to traditional 門. This written-form relationship does not transfer the received phonetic analysis of traditional 問 to the simplified graph.

sound_limitation.text: The current Mandarin readings can be compared, but do not establish a historical phonetic role for 门 in 问.

sound.text: In Modern Mandarin, 门 is mén and 问 is wèn; this current pair does not establish their historical relationship.

history.text: The selected image is a modern vector redraw in Shuowen-style seal script. It illustrates the received form of 問 but is not an excavated artifact or proof of a graphic sequence from the disputed Shang forms.

Two Shang graphs combining 門 and 口 were traditionally catalogued as 問. Their identification and descent from the later 問 graph are disputed; one tentative alternative is that they are expanded forms of 啟, but their inscriptional meaning remains unclear.

The earliest clear graph for the word meaning “ask” or “inquire” in the surveyed evidence is reported in late Warring States Qin slips. Earlier graphs read as 聞 or 昏 were also used to write the spoken word 問. This may be borrowing: a written sign can be reused for a different word when the words sound alike or similar, but the specific sound match between 聞 or 昏 and 問 is not established here. This is a proposed explanation for those writings, not a demonstrated sound history.
A separate proposal derives the spoken word 問 from 聞 with an exoactive suffix, roughly “let me hear.” This proposed word history is distinct from the use of 聞 or 昏 graphs to write 問.

uncertainties.text: The identity and meaning of the Shang 門-and-口 graphs, and their relationship to 問, remain disputed. The suggestion that they are expanded forms of 啟 is tentative.

The received analysis assigns 門 a phonetic role, but the available comparisons do not independently establish its historical sound correspondence with 問. The proposed derivation from 聞 plus a suffix is also unverified.
The late Warring States Qin-slip examples and their precise chronology are reported through a scholarly discussion; the primary slip records were not checked here.

senses.period: Late Warring States, as reported for the earliest clear graph in the surveyed evidence
senses.text: The earliest clear graph for the word meaning “ask” or “inquire” in the surveyed evidence is reported in late Warring States Qin slips. The received Shuowen gloss 訊 supports this meaning but does not itself establish the earliest use.

senses.gloss: discuss, investigate, interrogate, visit, give, and uses glossed as 通聞
senses.text: Historical dictionaries list these additional uses. Their dates and pathways from “ask” or “inquire,” or from one another, are not established, so they cannot be arranged as a sequence.
Current definitions include “ask about” and “inquire after.”

limitations.text: The late Warring States dating and Qin-slip examples are reported through a scholarly discussion; the cited primary slip records were not checked here.
No dated sequence or supported path connects the additional dictionary-listed senses to “ask” or to one another.

overview.text: 问 means “ask” or “inquire” and is the simplified form of 問. In the received analysis of 問, 口 is linked with speech and 門 is assigned a sound role, though the available readings do not demonstrate that historical link.

components.text: In traditional 問, 口 is the meaning element and links the character with speech.
The traditional analysis assigns 門 a sound role, though the available readings do not demonstrate the historical link to 問.
门 is the simplified form corresponding to traditional 門 in 问.

relationships.text: The received historical analysis assigns 口 the semantic role in 問.

The received analysis identifies 門 as 問’s phonetic component. Modern Mandarin gives mén and wèn; Baxter–Sagart gives *mˤə[r] and *C.mu[n]-s in its Old Chinese system. These comparisons do not independently establish the historical correspondence.
问 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 問, with 門 written as 门.
